raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #62939. With DSpark adaptive verification, startup can crash when `max_num_seqs * num_query_per_req` exceeds `max_num_batched_tokens`. The issue's command (Qwen3-8B, `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`) on main:

```
Assertion `index out of bounds: 0 <= tl.broadcast_to(tmp29, [XBLOCK, R0_BLOCK]) < 40960` failed.
...
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 1133, in capture_model
    self._dummy_run(**batch)
...
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

`_dummy_run` caps requests at `max_num_batched_tokens // num_query_per_req` so the draft pass fits its buffers (#56448). But adaptive verification's startup profiling replays varlen decode graphs padded to `max_num_seqs` requests, and the drafter drafts for every padded slot: up to 256 * 7 query rows against 512-row buffers (#58984 clamps this only for DP > 1). This PR pads those graphs only up to the same cap, which the scheduler already enforces (#59468); configs where the cap does not bind are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR targets #62939; #53970 takes a different route, growing the drafter buffers and the default budget.

## Validation

1x A100-80GB, base 6ee316eaea, Qwen3-8B + `dspark_qwen3_8b_block7`, `TRITON_ATTN`:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| the issue's `vllm serve` command | device-side assert at startup | starts, answers a chat request |
| 96 greedy chat requests at 512 | - | all complete, acceptance length 3.73 |
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 1792` (cap does not bind) | 51 varlen decode graphs | identical |

```
$ pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py::test_dspark_adaptive_verification_with_small_token_budget
# main: the same device-side assert as above, then
E               RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
======================== 1 failed, 1 warning in 26.76s =========================
# this PR
======================== 1 passed, 1 warning in 47.17s =========================
$ pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py \
    tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
65 passed in 59.86s
```

The new CPU test fails if either the request cap or its matching token bound is reverted. The e2e test runs in the nightly `Spec Decode AL DSpark` job and is skipped on ROCm, where it is untested.

All GPU runs above used the first revision (01d0d0b, on 6ee316eaea). Since then #63406 has reworked how varlen decode graph sizes are chosen, so the cap now sits in its varlen branch with the same logic (now on 2a777ce26e), and the unit test expects that branch's token grid.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+    """Dummy runs replay a varlen decode graph with every request slot filled.
+    When a DFlash/DSpark draft pass fits fewer requests than max_num_seqs, the
+    graphs must pad to that limit instead, and sizes that many requests cannot
+    fill get no varlen graph."""
+    manager = _make_spec_decode_manager(
+        monkeypatch,
+        capture_sizes=[1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24],
+        varlen_decode=True,
+        max_varlen_decode_reqs=4,
+    )
+

+        (desc.num_tokens, desc.num_reqs)
+        for desc in manager._capture_descs[CUDAGraphMode.FULL]
+    ] == [(12, 4), (10, 4), (8, 4), (4, 4), (2, 2), (1, 1)]
+
+    # A full decode step at the request cap still replays a FULL graph.
+    desc = manager.dispatch(
+        num_reqs=4,
+        num_tokens=4 * _DECODE_QUERY_LEN,
+        uniform_token_count=None,
+        num_active_loras=0,
+        max_query_len=_DECODE_QUERY_LEN,
+    )
+    assert desc.cg_mode == CUDAGraphMode.FULL
